source_text: Compendiis pauculorum uerborum quot attinguntur edicta prophetarum, euangeliorum, apostolorum, sermones domini, parabolae, exempla, praecepta! quot simul expunguntur officia! dei honor in patre, fidei testimonium in nomine, oblatio obsequii in uoluntate, commemoratio spei in regno, petitio uitae in pane, exomologesis debitorum in deprecatione, sollicitudo temptationum in postulatione tutelae. quid mirum? deus solus docere potuit, quomodo se uellet orari. ab ipso igitur ordinata religio orationis et de spiritu ipsius iam tunc cum ex ore diuino ferretur, animata suo priuilegio ascendit in caelum commendans patri quae filius docuit.
thought_title: The Lord's Prayer as a compendium of all duty
orientation: Tertullian has just begun his treatise by praising the Lord's Prayer as a summary of the whole gospel, and now he enumerates the duties it covers in each petition.
pass_a_gloss: By the compendiums of a very few words, how many edicts of the prophets, of the gospels, of the apostles, discourses of the Lord, parables, examples, precepts are touched upon! How many duties are at the same time discharged! The honor of God in the Father, the testimony of faith in the name, the offering of obedience in the will, the remembrance of hope in the kingdom, the petition of life in the bread, the confession of debts in the deprecation, the anxiety of temptations in the request for protection. What wonder? God alone could have taught how he wished himself to be prayed to. Therefore the religion of prayer was ordered by him himself, and, animated by the spirit of him himself, already then when it was being carried forth from the divine mouth, it ascended into heaven by its own privilege, commending to the Father the things which the Son taught.

lemmas.gloss: in the deprecation, plea for pardon

choices.why: Keeps the rhetorical force of the opening ablative of means; Tertullian is saying the Lord's Prayer is a summary that touches all these things.
The verb means to strike off or settle an account; 'discharged' preserves the sense of duties being fulfilled and crossed off.
Oblatio is a sacrificial term; keeping 'offering' preserves the cultic register Tertullian uses for prayer.
The glossary requires 'confession' for exomologesis and 'debts' for debita; this keeps both fixed terms.
Sollicitudo means anxious concern or care; 'anxiety' preserves the emotional weight, and 'temptations' follows the glossary.
Religio here means the ordered system of worship; 'religion' keeps the institutional sense Tertullian intends.

pass_b_english: In the compass of a very few words, how many sayings of the prophets, the gospels, the apostles are touched upon—the Lord's own discourses, parables, examples, commands! How many duties are discharged at once! The honor of God in the Father, the testimony of faith in the name, the offering of obedience in the will, the remembrance of hope in the kingdom, the petition for life in the bread, the confession of debts in the plea for pardon, the anxiety of temptations in the request for protection. What wonder is there in this? God alone could teach how he wished to be prayed to. Therefore the religion of prayer was established by him, and from his Spirit—already at that moment when it was being carried forth from the divine mouth—it was given life, and by its own privilege it ascends into heaven, commending to the Father what the Son taught.
